ledger.claim: The waiting-time fee of $5.00 is chargeable only where the trip was completed and the driver's in-geofence dwell before the rider boarded exceeded the free waiting period in force. The free waiting period for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), and the driver's own trace shows a continuous in-geofence dwell of only 100 seconds - a shortfall of 80 seconds. Under POL-NS-10(d) the waiting-time fee is not chargeable, and under POL-NS-10(e) the fare_breakdown waiting-time line must be refunded in full.

The effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period in force. The trace shows a single qualifying in-geofence run of 100 seconds (11 fixes, from 09:11:59 to 09:13:39), against a required minimum of 180 seconds for a STANDARD zone. The shortfall is 80 seconds. Under POL-NS-06 the waiting fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present.

The trip_record's own wait_timer_started event at 09:12:01 records a free waiting period of 180 seconds, and the trip was terminated at 09:43:59 - but the driver's GPS trace shows he left the pickup geofence at 09:13:39, only 100 seconds after the timer started. The platform's own telemetry and the GPS trace agree that the driver did not hold position for the required free waiting period. The waiting fee is therefore not chargeable under POL-NS-01 limb (c), which requires a continuous dwell of at least the free waiting period measured from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix.

The rider sent a message at 09:12:19 saying 'coming' - a coordinating message during the waiting window. The driver neither replied in the chat_log within 120 seconds nor placed an in-app voice call (trip_record.in_app_calls is empty). The rider's own track places her device within the 100 m rider presence radius for STANDARD zone for the majority of qualifying fixes (241 rider fixes, all at 0.0 kph, mean distance 3.9 m from the pin). Under POL-NS-04 the rider is exonerated and the fee refunded in full with no driver compensation payable.

The driver's arrival marker was a BUTTON press at 09:11:59, and the GPS trace places him at that moment inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius (min_distance_m 0.65 m, mean_distance_m 6831 m across the whole trip but the arrival fix is at the pin). The arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05 - the driver was stationary at the pin when he tapped. But the dwell that followed was only 100 seconds, so the fee fails on the dwell requirement, not on the arrival marker.

The fare_breakdown shows a waiting_time_fee of $5.00 charged on a completed trip, with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0. The rider contests exactly this $5.00. Since the dwell did not exceed the free waiting period, the waiting-time line is refunded in full under POL-NS-10(e). The cancellation_fee line is 0.0, so no cancellation fee is in issue.

The traffic advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-02740-01 is MISSING - no advisory covers Blk 108 Yishun Ring Rd in this window. Under POL-NS-06 limb (i), a MISSING traffic_advisory makes the accumulation limb unavailable: the driver cannot rely on a kerb restriction or enforcement operation to sum separate in-geofence intervals. The single 100-second run stands as the whole dwell, and the shortfall is not excused.

ledger.claim: The rider's profile shows no_show_disputes_30d of 0 and disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0, and the driver's profile shows no_show_terminations_30d of 0 and disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0. Neither the POL-NS-09(c) repeat-dispute trigger nor the POL-NS-09(d) abuse trigger is engaged. The case is decidable on the evidence and does not require escalation.

The trip record shows the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 09:11:59 and the platform started a free waiting period of 180 seconds at 09:12:01, but the trip was terminated by completion at 09:43:59 with no cancellation_reason_code and no rider no-show event anywhere in the record. POL-NS-01 limb (d) requires the trip to be terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE or EXCESSIVE_WAIT; the record shows cancellation_reason_code null and cancelled_by null, so limb (d) fails and the no-show fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01.

The rider's own message 'coming' was sent at 09:12:19 and read at 09:12:29, and the driver never replied in the chat log nor placed any in-app voice call (trip_record.in_app_calls is empty). Under POL-NS-04 limbs (a) and (b) the rider sent a coordinating message during the waiting window and the driver neither replied within 120 seconds nor called, so the rider is exonerated and the fee is refunded in full with no driver compensation.

The rider's device track places the rider within the STANDARD-zone rider presence radius of 100 m for the majority of qualifying fixes across the waiting window: rider_presence shows 241 fixes with a maximum distance of 7.36 m from the pickup pin and a mean of 3.90 m, all at 0.0 kph. POL-NS-04 limb (c) is therefore affirmatively satisfied on admissible fixes, completing the rider-exoneration test.

The driver's own trace shows a longest qualifying in-geofence run of only 100 seconds, from 09:11:59 to 09:13:39, against the STANDARD-zone minimum dwell of 180 seconds set by POL-NS-01(c) and the fee schedule. The shortfall is 80 seconds, so the effective dwell is shorter than the free waiting period in force and POL-NS-06 requires the cancellation fee to be refunded in full whether or not the rider was present.

The waiting-time fee of $5.00 on the fare breakdown is not supported: POL-NS-10(d) makes a waiting-time fee chargeable only where the trip was completed and the driver's in-geofence dwell before the rider boarded exceeded free_wait_sec, and the measured dwell here is 100 seconds against a 180-second free waiting period. Under POL-NS-10(e) the unsupported waiting-time line is refunded in full.

The fare breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00 and a waiting_time_fee line of $5.00, so the contested amount is presently standing against the rider and a refund of that line is the remedy the policy provides. The charge is not a cancellation fee but a waiting-time fee, and POL-NS-10(e) is the clause that reaches it.

The driver's arrival marker is a BUTTON press, not a platform-confirmed GPS_AUTO arrival, so POL-NS-12 does not apply and the arrival and dwell must be tested against the exported trace under POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-05. The trace is complete at 100.0% coverage with 10-second sampling and no gaps, so the 100-second dwell reading is reliable and not an artifact of sparse data.

The traffic advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-02740-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and no payload, so POL-NS-06 limb (i) cannot be used to accumulate dwell across intervals: the limb requires a present and populated traffic_advisory of type KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT, and a MISSING advisory makes the limb unavailable. The 100-second dwell therefore stands as the effective dwell with no accumulation.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you: this dispute is about the $5.00 waiting-time fee on trip TRP-02740, and that fee cannot stand. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02740) shows a waiting_time_fee line of $5.00, a cancellation_fee line of $0.00 and a total_charged of $33.23, with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00; the $5.00 is the contested amount, and it is the only charge in issue. / POL-NS-10(d) makes a waiting-time fee chargeable only where the trip was completed and the driver's in-geofence dwell before the rider boarded, measured as POL-NS-01(c) measures it, exceeded the free waiting period in force. The free waiting period for this trip is 180 seconds, read from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec (EV-TRIP-02740). The driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-02740), which is complete (100.0% coverage, 10-second sampling, no gaps), shows a single continuous in-geofence run from 09:11:59 to 09:13:39 - 100 seconds - because the driver left the geofence when the trip started at 09:13:39. The shortfall against the 180-second minimum is 80 seconds. The platform's own wait timer began at 09:12:01 (EV-TRIP-02740) but the driver did not hold position for the period the timer measured. POL-NS-10(e) therefore requires the unsupported waiting-time line to be refunded in full: $5.00 back to the rider. The independent POL-NS-06 shortfall argument and the POL-NS-01(c) dwell argument run to the same figure and are accepted. / Both advocates' points on the arrival marker are accepted: the marker is a driver BUTTON press, so POL-NS-12 does not apply and the exported trace governs (EV-TRIP-02740, EV-GPS-02740); and the tap was made with the driver at the pin, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, so the marker is not false under POL-NS-05 and no false-arrival referral is produced by that clause. / On the driver's side, no compensation is due. POL-NS-01 does not apply in full: limb (d) requires the trip to be terminated by the driver with a no-show reason code, but this trip was completed normally at 09:43:59 with cancellation_reason_code null and cancelled_by null (EV-TRIP-02740), and no cancellation fee was charged on the ledger. POL-NS-07 has nothing to pay out for that reason. The anti-farming check is nevertheless not tripped (driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d 0, completed_trips_30d 67), and no POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is engaged (rider no_show_disputes_30d 0 and disputes_with_counterparty_90d 0 on both profiles), so the case is decidable on the record. / The rider's POL-NS-04 arguments (the coordinating message 'coming' at 09:12:19, unanswered, with no in-app call, and the rider's device within the 100 m STANDARD presence radius) point the same way, but the refund here flows from POL-NS-10(e). The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02740-01 is absent from the record; no accumulation of separate in-geofence intervals is required because only one interval exists, so the advisory does not affect the outcome in either direction. No clause produces a referral or an escalation on these facts. Confidence is 0.95, within the cap of 1.0 set by the artifacts that carry the deciding dwell fact (EV-GPS-02740 and EV-TRIP-02740, each at weight 1.0).

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
